title: Motion Design - A Murder of Crows
description: The brief for this project was to create a short motion design animation based on a concept of our choice. The final piece needed to communicate a clear idea through motion, timing, and visual storytelling.

I chose to base my animation on the phrase “a murder of crows“. Using hand-drawn illustrations, a limited black-and-white color palette, and subtle animation, I created an eerie atmosphere that plays on the phrase's double meaning. The animation gradually reveals the full phrase through the arrival of the crows, combining illustration and motion to tell a simple visual story.

The bouncing cat animation was created as a variation of the classic bouncing ball exercise. The focus was on applying animation principles such as timing, anticipation, and squash and stretch while adding a simple character element.

The Scoops Ice Cream animation was created using provided assets for a fictional advertising campaign. The project focused on using motion to support a voice-over, creating clear visual communication while maintaining a simple and approachable style.

title: Magnetic Magazine - Magazine Design
description: The brief for this project was to design and lay out a printed edition of Magnetic Magazine, including a cover, table of contents, about page, and four feature articles. The challenge was to create a cohesive editorial design that reflected the magazine's existing brand while remaining engaging and easy to navigate.

I created a magazine inspired by music production and the progressive music culture that Magnetic Magazine covers. The cover features a custom illustration, while the interior uses a grid-based layout, clear typographic hierarchy, and color-coded article categories to improve navigation. The design combines clean layouts, strong typography, and visual consistency to create a magazine that feels connected to the existing digital brand.

title: Photography - Clarity
description: The brief for this project was to create an advertisement for a fictional product or service using a self-produced photograph. The image had to combine model photography with either architectural, landscape, or astro photography, with the model as the main focus of the composition.

I created an advertisement for a fictional mental wellness app called Clarity. The photograph combines a blurred model with the architecture of Kilden Performing Arts Centre to visually represent mental overwhelm and the search for clarity. The contrast between the moving figure and the structured surroundings reinforces the concept, while a minimal layout and the tagline “Slow your mind.” support the calm and focused message of the app.

title: BUGS - Packaging Design
description: A visual identity and packaging design for BUGS, a chocolate snack targeting Gen Z. The brief was to create a name, logo, packaging, social media content, and a poster to communicate the product's playful gaming theme and ethical cocoa sourcing.

I developed a pixel-inspired logo and glitch patterns across packaging and digital content. The packaging features a resealable box for convenient snacking while gaming. A vibrant color palette, playful pixel illustrations, and custom characters engage the audience while icons and layout highlight the brand's principles. The project ensures clarity, brand recognition, and appealing aesthetics across multiple touchpoints.

title: Mindre Matsvinn - Awareness Campaign
description: An awareness campaign for children aged 6-10 to promote responsible food consumption. The brief was to develop a mascot, posters, a folder, and a style manual that educate while remaining engaging for young audiences.

I created Finn, a raccoon mascot, and used a bright and playful color palette with illustrations and layouts that visually communicate tips for reducing food waste. The posters and folder combine educational content with fun and interactive elements. The campaign emphasizes clarity, consistency, and appeal, making the message memorable for children.

title: Summefestivalen - Brand Identity, Marketing material and Packaging
description: A complete visual identity for Summefestivalen, a festival celebrating World Bee Day at Kaldvell Gård. The brief was to create a cohesive brand identity across logo, app, and packaging for festival honey.

The identity uses organic shapes, warm colors, and hand-drawn botanical elements to reflect nature, sustainability, and a family-friendly atmosphere. The app extends the festival experience digitally with recipes, maps, and news, while the honey packaging combines hexagonal forms and eco-friendly materials. The final design balances visual consistency with engagement for families, students, and sustainability-minded audiences.

title: Unanswered - Awareness Campaign
description: A campaign focused on the gender gap in healthcare, highlighting how women's symptoms are often dismissed and research is male-focused. The brief was to develop a visual identity, poster series, billboards, and interactive touchpoint cards to raise awareness among young women.

The branding is minimal and bold, using black, white, and Unanswered Red to communicate missing information. The logo combines the female symbol with a question mark and reinforces the slogan, “Women deserve answers.” The poster series balances personal stories and statistical information, while the cards offer a tangible, interactive way to engage. The campaign materials are consistent, clear, and memorable.

title: CuteCon - Branding, Website & Social Media
description: A fictional convention celebrating all things cute, from kawaii fashion and plushies to cosplay and creative workshops. The brief was to develop a visual identity, mascots, a mobile site prototype, and social media content to engage attendees.

The branding uses pastel colors, rounded fonts, and playful mascots to reflect inclusivity, creativity, and fun. The mobile site prioritizes intuitive navigation and ticket purchase, while social media content reinforces engagement and entertainment. The project balances professionalism with playful charm, creating a cohesive and recognizable identity for fans, creators, and families.

title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban - Book Cover Redesign
description: A book cover redesign giving a more mature and mysterious interpretation of Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban. The brief was to create a cover that appeals to adults familiar with the series while reflecting the story's themes.

The cover centers on an hourglass containing key story elements, with two Dementors forming the silhouette of Sirius Black's dog. I used a monochromatic green palette and Celtic MN for the title to reference the series' mythological roots. The layout guides the eye toward the hourglass while keeping the composition clear and focused, balancing symbolism and visual clarity.

images.desc: Mockup of the new cover I designed for Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban.

title: Nexa - Brand Identity
description: A full brand identity for Nexa, a high-end tech brand targeting nostalgic millennials. The brief was to create a brand that merges modern technology with playful Y2K-inspired design.

The logo features a star icon inside the “A” referencing retro-futuristic aesthetics, while the color palette balances purple, cyan, yellow, black, and gray to combine playfulness and sophistication. Typography is SF Pro, using Expanded Black for headlines and Regular for body text. Mockups show packaging, posters, and a mobile-first website, and the Time Machine pop-up creates an immersive, nostalgic experience with interactive displays of late-90s/00s gadgets alongside Nexa products.

title: Designfestivalen - Folder
description: An informational folder for a fictional pop-up exhibition organized by Kunstsiloen, celebrating three graphic design eras: Bauhaus, Modernism, and Postmodernism. The brief was to create a folder that communicates each era and key designers clearly for adult audiences.

The folder presents Herbert Bayer, Paul Rand, and Paula Scher, highlighting their signature styles. I used a “Stepped Accordion” fold to make each section title visible when closed, and a consistent typographic approach with Neue Kabel. Colors and layout reflect each era while maintaining visual cohesion across the folder.

title: Photography - 15 Principles
description: A series of 15 photographs exploring key photography principles using manual camera settings. The brief was to experiment with shutter speed, aperture, and ISO to create visually engaging images that demonstrate each principle.

I captured images indoors and outdoors using natural light, props, and models to explore movement, perspective, and composition. Each image was composed to highlight the chosen principle. The photobook presents the images with a consistent layout and typography.

title: Skumle Dager - New logo for Dyreparken
description: A logo redesign for “Skumle Dager,” a Halloween event with three distinct experiences for different age groups. The brief was to create a cohesive visual identity that distinguishes each experience while maintaining a clear connection across the event.

I designed a central umbrella logo with playful, spooky colors and integrated a tree motif into the typography to reflect the forested setting of the park. The logo was applied across mockups and a style manual to ensure consistency.

title: A Tail Through Graphic Design History - Leaflet Design
description: A folded leaflet designed for a pop-up exhibition exploring four graphic design movements: Swiss Style, Pop Art, Psychedelic Poster Style, and Punk / New Wave. The brief was to create an engaging and educational souvenir that communicates each style clearly to adult viewers.

To create cohesion between very different styles, I used a shared color palette and a recurring cat motif. The cat's tail functions as a timeline connecting the eras, while each section reinterprets the same subject through its own visual language. The leaflet balances unity and contrast across typography, color, and composition, making it both informative and memorable.

title: Product Photography - Candle
description: A product photoshoot highlighting the Wooden House scented candle from Nille. The brief was to communicate warmth, elegance, and minimalism through photography.

The sleek black packaging contrasts with a dark background, while warm, painterly light evokes a cozy, homely atmosphere. Lighting was created using phone screens and a small flashlight with long exposure, shaping highlights and emphasizing texture. The composition uses a simple wooden prop to connect to the scent, keeping the focus on the product. The images communicate both luxurious and comforting qualities.
